28.text: HAIR-DRESSING. — Many of the Chukchee men cut the hair on the crown

29.text: of the head as close as possible, so that it looks almost as if shaven, forming

30.text: a kind of tonsure (see Plate XXIX, Fig. 4). The hair around the tonsure is

31.text: trimmed to look like fringe, sometimes in a double row (Plate XXX, Fig. 3).
31.note: Roman numeral printed lower-case (xxx) on the page; keyed ASCII capitals per §2.12.

32.text: On top of the head, on both sides of the tonsure, two long locks are left by

33.text: some of the men. These locks look not unlike the ears of an animal. The

34.text: fashion of wearing a tonsure is in use also among the Koryak and among

35.text: the Asiatic and American Eskimo. Among the Chukchee it is of late years

36.text: gradually being superseded by the ordinary style of hair-cut.

37.text: The tonsure and fringe are resorted to whenever it is thought necessary,

38.text: for superstitious reasons, to change one’s appearance. For instance, a person

39.text: thus protects himself from the spirits of contagious diseases, or a murderer

40.text: conceals his identity from the revengeful soul of his victim. From the same

41.text: motive, usually on command of shamans, men may allow their hair to grow,

42.text: and plait it in braids after the fashion of women, or leave a few locks on

43.text: the temples or on the back of the neck, to be plaited into a small braid.
